The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. #4317. Palworld Dev Gives Employees an Official GTA6 Vacation Week

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

We are officially… let me check my calendar here… one week out from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. The hatches are being battened down, evacuations are underway, toilet paper is sold out across the world. We’re looking at a Category 5-hype video game release here, and everyone waits with bated breath for the moment to arrive.

For about as long as the game’s official release date has been known, prospective players have been planning their time off, whether they get it formally approved by their employers, or they just plan to spontaneously develop a virulent cold and call in sick. Offices, schools, and just about every other public place will be virtually empty as the world screeches to a halt on November 19.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is releasing exactly one day before the official nomination cutoff date for the 2026 Game Awards.

With all that in mind, if everyone is going to take time off or sick days anyway, the sporting thing to do would be to just make it official. This is the avenue that the developer of popular creature-collect and crafting survival game Palworld, Pocketpair, is taking with its employees; as the company announced in a tweet on the official Palworld X, formerly Twitter account, everyone working for it will be getting five days off from work for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

As the tweet on the Palworld account reads, “All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches.”

This was followed by an image showing a statement on what I’m assuming is official Pocketpair company stationary, which reads, “on November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin.”

“At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention.”

All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches.

The note then announces that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto 6 will be granted a special five-day holiday running from Thursday, November 19 to Monday, November 23, which also provides enough time to fly to Miami for the game's big release festival. The note adds that only those who intend to actually play GTA6 are eligible for this time off, though considering the nature of this break, I kind of doubt that’ll actually be enforced.

The note also adds, presumably for the sake of end users, that update work for Palworld and Craftopia is currently on schedule and will be carried out as normal.

Logitech wants employees to reap the personal and professional benefits of gaming.

The note concludes with a well-wish for employees, reading, “we hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels.”

This is a very sporting thing for Pocketpair to do, not to mention a pretty amusing way to go about it. Honestly, though, it would probably behoove many companies in the game industry, and indeed, the entire United States business sector, to follow suit.

When I said before that the world will grind to a halt on November 19, that wasn’t an exaggeration. Last month, an economics professor at Pompeu Fabra University in Barcelona, José García Montalvo, spoke to the International Business Times, providing an estimate of how much money the U.S. economy will lose due to people taking vacation, calling in sick, or otherwise skipping work on GTA6 release day. With a rough estimate of 1.5 million absences, based on an average annual income of $70,000, Montalvo ballparks that this single day will cost the U.S. economy roughly $1 billion in lost productivity.

There’s even a precedent for this within the greater GTA legacy, as when Grand Theft Auto 5 released in 2013, approximately 6% of all working adults aged 18 to 35 in major metropolitan U.S. cities took the day off.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to be one of the biggest drops in gaming history, and Take-Two is looking to bag some seriously stacked cash.

#4315. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4313. Neil Druckmann Says Intergalactic is ‘Playable’, But Don’t Expect More This Year

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

Naughty Dog has been keeping Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet under wraps for quite some time, and fans hoping for a surprise gameplay reveal before the end of the year might want to temper their expectations (and yes, that’s also a self-note).

Its creative director Neil Druckmann, best known for creating The Last of Us, has finally offered an update on the studio's upcoming sci-fi adventure, confirming that the game is now playable and entering its final stages of production. But sadly, that doesn't mean we're getting a closer look at it anytime soon.

During a recent appearance at Comic Creators Block Party 2026, Druckmann spoke with host Patton Oswalt about the project, which was first announced at The Game Awards in December 2024. While he was careful not to reveal too much, he did share that the development team has reached an important milestone.

“We’re kind of at the last stage of production, where we can play it, and we’re refining and polishing it, and I can’t wait to show it to the world,” Druckmann explained.

MGS, Uncharted, Halo, and Assassin's Creed veteran, Robin Atkins Downes, is joining the cast of Intergalactic, Naughty Dog's new title.

That's certainly encouraging news, especially considering how little we've seen of Intergalactic since its initial reveal. However, players shouldn't mistake this update for a sign that Naughty Dog is preparing to release the game in the near future.

Druckmann actually reiterated something that Naughty Dog already confirmed back in September this year: they will remain quiet about Intergalactic for the rest of 2026, with a full reveal planned for sometime next year. According to the creative director, the team will show “a lot” of the game in 2027, including gameplay and more of its story. He also teased that the final experience might surprise people, particularly those who think they already have a good idea of what Intergalactic will be.

Druckmann actually reiterated something that Naughty Dog already confirmed back in September this year: they will remain quiet about Intergalactic for the rest of 2026, with a full reveal planned for sometime next year.

Considering that the first trailer mostly introduced protagonist Jordan A. Mun and the game's mysterious sci-fi setting, there's still plenty Naughty Dog hasn't shown us! And, honestly, after waiting this long, a proper gameplay showcase sounds like the least we can ask for.

Neil Druckmann announced that this isn't the last we've seen of The Last of Us, with two new projects already in development.

Besides, Druckmann also offered a little more insight into the creative direction behind Intergalactic, describing it as a combination of three of Naughty Dog's biggest franchises. He explained that the studio wanted to return to sci-fi and fantasy after spending so much time working on the relatively grounded worlds of Uncharted and The Last of Us.

For that, the team is drawing inspiration from the sci-fi and fantasy elements of Jak and Daxter, the pulpy action-adventure style of Uncharted that we all miss deeply, and the more serious drama found in The Last of Us. He also highlighted the studio's ambition to expand its gameplay systems, asking whether Naughty Dog could maintain the cinematic storytelling it's known for while offering deeper gameplay mechanics.

That's an interesting combination for sure, especially for a studio that has spent much of the last decade focusing on cinematic adventures. So we still have no release date for Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, but at least 2027 is shaping up to be the year we'll finally understand what the studio has been working on.

#4312. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. #4311. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4306. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

Invictus Gaming are through to the last four of Worlds 2026. They beat fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening match of the Knockout Stage. The series was played at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas, on 3 November (US time).

#4300. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4298. Laid-Off Id Software Employees Form their Own Studio, Hidden Horses

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

2026 has been home to a swath of large-scale layoffs throughout the gaming industry, mostly in the western sector. A statistically-significant portion of these layoffs have come from Microsoft, which has been systematically pruning many of its subsidiaries, including some of its highest-profile studios like id Software and Bethesda. Obviously, this is terrible for the many, many developers who worked for those studios, but some of those same developers have decided to turn this pinch into a chance.

Xbox cut 3,200 jobs. The developers who lost theirs explain what that actually means for the games that were supposed to come next.

Today, a coalition of developers who were specifically laid off from id Software following their work on Doom: The Dark Ages announced the formation of their new independent studio: Hidden Horses. If that name is a reference to something, I don’t know what it is, but what this studio may lack in readily-apparent branding, it more than makes up for in the crew of talented, highly-experienced developers it consists of.

According to Hidden Horses’s newly-created website, this independent studio wants to make games “like it was done in the 90’s,” with an emphasis on carefully hand-crafted gaming experiences tailored by longtime industry veterans. The studio’s first project is already in progress, with plans to bring it to life via crowdfunding in the near future.

While these industry vets have lost the ample funding that comes with a major backer like Microsoft, they have, in turn, gained substantial freedom in how they pursue their projects. This is one of the stated benefits of the studio’s formation, as outlined on the “How We Work” section of the Hidden Horses website.

“The company was created as a developer run and owned studio,” the page reads. “This allows us to pursue fun and creativity in our games, unencumbered by short-term thinking or chasing market trends.”

They have gained substantial freedom in how they pursue their projects.

The team considers this structure optimal because helps them make games right, rather than make them quickly, creating new and interesting gameplay concepts rather than trying to flip half-baked products for a quick buck. The team is firmly of the belief that, despite changes in the industry and players, there is still very much a demand for the kinds of carefully-designed games that they’re accustomed to creating.

After being cut off by its previous publisher, Romero Games has secured a fresh bout of funding and refocused with a smaller dev team.

The page also notes that the studio will be run democratically, with input from every member of the team on all important business decisions, all to ensure nobody gets left out in the cold. “We do this not only because we think it is fair, but because we think it is a better way to run a business.”

Despite having just formed, Hidden Horses already has irons in the fire. On the “Our First Project” page of the website, the studio outlines its plans for its very first game development project. This game, titled Danger Pay, will be a “high-octane single-player FPS” set in a malevolent, futuristic game show in a manner reminiscent of Smash TV and The Running Man.

“Our game will focus on classic FPS gameplay, awesome weapons, crazy enemies, and will be highly optimized.”

Of course, financial backing for an entirely new game project doesn’t come out of nowhere, which is why the plan for this first project is to fund it via Kickstarter. A page for Danger Pay has already been created, though there’s no word yet on when the campaign will actually begin.

“We believe that the community around the type of games we have helped develop is robust, and we invite all supporters to join us in trying to create something special,” the Kickstarter description reads. “This will include the typical things needed to start a business and finance a game's development - licenses, hardware, healthcare, etc. Our goal will be based around the timeline of our first project and associated costs.”

You can now experience Wyldheart, the upcoming co-op RPG from former AAA developers, for yourself.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4293. Jensen Huang’s Departure from NVIDIA Sparks Hope of a Gaming Pivot

Contributor at DualShockers, former Esports Insider DACH content lead, former Escapist Magazine Germany content lead, software engineering background.

NVIDIA has announced that co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO whilst continuing as CFO, with Harvey Jones becoming the board’s first-ever chair. The announcement didn’t give a reason, although it obviously arrived after very public reports of extramarital affairs, one of them reportedly with a woman US intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy. Neither NVIDIA nor Huang has confirmed the reporting, but investors reacted regardless, with shares falling as much as 14% at the open.

Masato Kumzawa addresses fan reactions to Grace Ashcroft's design and the impact of NVIDIA's DLSS 5 AI technology.

Ultimately, I’m not that interested in the gossip. What interests me far more is what happens to a company that has spent the last few years being defined by one man’s bet on AI, and whether that opens the door for the side of the business that first made NVIDIA a household name. For anyone who has tried to buy a graphics card recently, that is a rather important question.

Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and ran it for more than 33 years, with the move into AI being very much his decision. It has paid off enormously, because data centres now make up roughly 91.5% of the company’s revenue. The flip side is that nobody else has been quite as closely tied to that strategy, which makes for some interesting possibilities for NVIDIA’s future.

Kress has been CFO since 2013 and is a well-respected voice with the market, and eToro’s Josh Gilbert described her as a familiar and trusted presence, whilst adding that a company known for its technical edge might want an engineer in the chair. Analyst Dan Ives expects her stint as interim CEO to last around a year before NVIDIA looks outside. NVIDIA’s company structure is interesting in that it doesn’t make finding a solution any easier: Huang had more than 60 people reporting to him directly.

NVIDIA has no COO, and reports suggest there was no succession plan in place. The internal names analysts have put forward, such as Ian Buck, Bill Dally, Michael Kagan and Bryan Catanzaro, are largely AI and data centre figures, but none of them has been the face of the strategy in the way Huang was. Constellation Research’s Ray Wang pointed out that many of NVIDIA’s partnerships and investments came about because people trusted Jensen.

Which brings me to the hopium. NVIDIA started out making graphics cards for gamers, and CNBC has pointed out that those gamers helped keep the company afloat back in 1999 by buying the GeForce 256. These days they account for under 10% of revenue, and it shows: RTX 50-series production was reportedly cut by up to 40% earlier this year, the Super refresh was reportedly shelved, and the next generation has reportedly drifted towards 2028. Meanwhile, the RTX 5090 launched at $1,999 and third-party sellers have been asking far more than that ever since.

Nvidia DLSS 5 is officially supported in 2K27, but eager fans have found their own way to enable the software in a myriad of titles.

So it isn’t hard to see why some gamers are hoping the board promotes someone with roots on that side of the business. Jeff Fisher, SVP of GeForce, has been at NVIDIA since 1994, but it is obvious that Kress is probably the safer bet for investors. Jonah Alben, who has led GPU engineering since 2008, and co-founder Chris Malachowsky might also throw a hat into this race. It is however important to note that all of this is still very much speculation: nobody at NVIDIA has hinted at a gaming pivot, and whether that will happen with any likeliness will be heavily dependent on other factors.

Truth be told, I wouldn’t expect a new CEO to change much straight away, even one with a soft spot for gaming. The memory shortage squeezing GeForce is affecting the entire industry, with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron reportedly prioritising AI customers for their high-bandwidth memory, and that won’t disappear because of who is sitting in the corner office.

Whoever takes over will also inherit a company that has just lost its founder and a fair amount of investor confidence, which tends to make boards cautious rather than adventurous. Even so, I’d quite like to see someone in charge who remembers where GeForce came from, and who has some sympathy for the people still trying to buy one. For now, Kress is running both the company and its finances whilst the search for a permanent CEO gets under way.

Between GTA 6's leaked pricing and the Steam Machine's $1,049 reveal, this week made one thing clear: gaming is getting expensive everywhere at once.

#4288. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4287. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4281. 10 Ocarina of Time Remake Changes That Break the Hearts of Nostalgic Fans

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has brought one of the most beloved and iconic adventures in gaming history back to life with a revamped visual presentation, plenty of gameplay improvements, and a surprising number of small changes that make exploring Hyrule feel fresh all over again. From quality-of-life improvements to the inventory and equipment systems to subtle environmental tweaks, there's literally a lot to appreciate about Nintendo's new take on this timeless classic.

However, as someone who grew up playing the original (and has an admittedly unhealthy amount of nostalgia running through my veins), I couldn't help but notice that some of the little things I loved are no longer around – or they are, but in a very different way.

Thomas Mahler believes Nintendo missed an opportunity to improve the level design in the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

Don't get me wrong, I absolutely adore this remake and described it as a lovely modern remake with an old soul, but that doesn't mean I'm not allowed to miss a few things from my childhood, right? So, please allow me to put my nostalgic glasses on for a moment and revisit ten changes that have left a tiny hole in my heart.

One of my favorite things about the original Ocarina of Time was starting a new save file and giving Link the most ridiculous name I could think of. It was such a simple feature, but it opened the door to some quite hilarious moments, especially when characters started addressing the legendary hero using whatever silly name I'd come up with.

One of my personal favorites was naming him “Bro.” Suddenly, every conversation in Hyrule sounded like everyone was part of the most laid-back adventure imaginable.

Unfortunately, the remake has decided to put an end to our creative freedom by locking the protagonist's name to Link. I can understand the reasoning, especially considering Nintendo's efforts to make the franchise more accessible to new generations and expand its presence across other media (since the live-action movie is coming hot). Still, I'll always miss my little adventures with Bro. You will be missed, buddy.

One of the coolest easter eggs in the original Ocarina of Time was hidden in the courtyard where you first meet Princess Zelda. As Child Link, you must sneak past the castle guards to reach the princess without getting caught. Once you've had your little chat with her, however, there's nothing stopping you from exploring the area and discovering a few fun secrets.

Among them is a window you can shoot with your Slingshot, prompting a particularly grumpy guard to throw a bomb in your direction (how rude!). But that's not all. If you look through the other windows, you'll find three familiar faces from the Super Mario universe: Mario, Luigi, and Bowser, all sporting their Super Mario 64 appearances.

I was honestly expecting Nintendo to bring this little crossover back using the characters' more modern designs, perhaps even their Super Mario Odyssey models. Instead, the entire reference has been removed from the remake. It's a shame, considering how charming these little Nintendo Easter eggs can be. At least the guard is still there to throw a bomb at your face. Some traditions must be preserved, I suppose.

If there's one thing every Ocarina of Time veteran knows, it's that Rupees are important, and there's no shame in taking advantage of a good farming opportunity. One of the earliest places where you could stock up on some extra cash was a room inside Hyrule Castle's Market, conveniently filled with breakable pots.

As Child Link, you could simply walk inside, smash everything in sight, collect the Rupees, leave, and come back to find the pots replenished. Rinse and repeat until your pockets were sufficiently full.

Unfortunately, the remake has decided that we shouldn't be allowed to get rich quite so easily. While you can still find some pots containing Rupees in the room, they no longer respawn simply by leaving the castle and coming back inside. Instead, you'll have to wait quite a while and spend some time doing other activities before they return. I guess we'll just have to go back to cutting grass like the rest of Hyrule's hardworking citizens.

I know what you're thinking – why on earth would anyone miss Kaepora Gaebora being annoying? But hear me out, I promise there's a reason behind my questionable opinion!

I also ain't a fan of the original owl. In fact, I probably spent more time than I'd like to admit accidentally answering “No” when he asked whether I wanted to hear his explanation again. And if you've played the original, you know exactly how frustrating that could be. However, there was something strangely entertaining about collectively hating this overly talkative bird. Kaepora became one of those characters that practically every Ocarina of Time player had a story about, and that shared frustration was part of the experience.

Now, the remake has given him a much cuter appearance, and he's also significantly less annoying, behaving much more like the wise and mysterious owl he's supposed to be. I mean, where’s the fun in that? I can't help missing the days when simply seeing him fly toward me filled me with dread.

Ocarina of Time has plenty of memorable exploit tricks, but one of my personal favorites involved getting a Heart Piece much earlier than Nintendo originally intended.

In the original game, you could perform a particularly well-timed backflip from the top of Death Mountain, near the entrance to Goron City, and land on the roof of Dodongo's Cavern. This allowed you to grab a Heart Piece that was normally intended for Adult Link, long before you were supposed to have access to it. It was just one of those silly little tricks that made exploring Hyrule feel even more rewarding.

Well, those days are over. The remake has adjusted the backflip's height, making it considerably less effective, and even tweaked the position of Dodongo's Cavern entrance to prevent players from pulling off the same trick (not that I tried to do it or anything).

From suspicious house designs to familiar songs, fans think they've found clues.

There's an unwritten rule among players: the moment you unlock the Hookshot, you must immediately equip it and start shooting at everything in sight. And one of your first destinations will probably be the rooftops of Kakariko Village.

This was really fun because it offered more freedom than simply using it to reach the obvious targets. You could experiment with different surfaces, discover unexpected ways to navigate the environment, and generally mess around with an incredibly useful piece of equipment. Apparently, however, that wasn't quite what Nintendo had in mind. The remake has restricted the Hookshot's functionality, meaning it can now only latch onto specific designated targets, such as stone markers and certain treasure chests.

I understand that this might have been done to prevent unintended shortcuts or make progression more controlled, but I can't help feeling that something has been lost in the process. One of the most enjoyable aspects of Ocarina of Time was experimenting with your equipment and discovering creative ways to use it. So, please, Nintendo, give us our old Hookshot back!

One of my most vivid childhood memories of Ocarina of Time involves something that probably sounds completely ridiculous to anyone who didn't grow up playing the original: stepping into Hyrule Field for the very first time and desperately running toward Hyrule Castle like a lunatic.

That happened because, if night fell before we reached the castle gates, they would close, leaving Link stranded outside until morning – and Hyrule Field at night was not exactly the safest place to be.

And you’ve guessed: the remake has removed this particular inconvenience, meaning you no longer have to worry about being locked out of Hyrule Castle after sunset. My adult self appreciates not having to deal with that little problem, but the child in me misses those frantic nighttime sprints.

There's something wonderfully weird about the little laboratory at Lake Hylia. Inside, you'll find a rather eccentric scientist who spends most of his time complaining about his back pain while standing next to a water tank.

He'll even offer you a reward if you manage to dive deep enough to touch the bottom of the pool. Naturally, being the helpful hero that you are, you'll want to give it a try. But once you reach the bottom, you'll discover something rather unexpected: a shark inside a cage.

What made this little discovery even funnier in the original game was the shark itself! Rather than featuring a detailed 3D model, it was represented by a hilariously low-resolution, static image. It looked so out of place that it became one of those bizarre little details you simply couldn't forget. While the remake has kept the shark in the aquarium, unfortunately, it has also given it a proper visual upgrade. Sure, it looks considerably better now, but I miss the ridiculous charm of that pixelated little creature.

If there's one thing Ocarina of Time does exceptionally well, it's turning a seemingly innocent adventure into a horror game without any warning! One moment you're exploring a dungeon and collecting treasures, and the next you're desperately running for your life from something that looks like it escaped from your worst nightmare.

Few enemies capture that feeling better than the Wallmaster, a giant disembodied hand that suddenly drops from the ceiling, grabs Link, and sends him all the way back to the beginning of the area or dungeon.

And what made this enemy so terrifying in the original was the anticipation. You couldn't simply look up to check whether it was coming, so you had to rely on an increasingly unsettling sound effect and the shadow that gradually appeared above Link. The remake preserves most of these elements, but introduces one rather important difference: a spotlight that illuminates the area whenever it’s about to appear. Combined with its shadow, this makes the enemy practically announce its arrival in the most dramatic way possible.

I appreciate the warning, but I honestly miss the uncertainty that made these encounters so frightening in the original. Thankfully, the Dead Hand is absolutely nightmare-inducing in the remake, so I'll let this one slide.

Remember the Water Temple? If you played the original Ocarina of Time back in the day, there's a good chance that simply reading those two words made you feel a little uncomfortable.

For years, this dungeon had a reputation for being one of the most frustrating experiences in the entire game. Between constantly changing the water level and switching between the Iron Boots and other equipment, it was enough to test even the most patient players.

There was also a particularly nasty Small Key hidden underneath the floor of the central pillar, which could only be accessed after raising the water level. It was incredibly easy to overlook, and if you ever found yourself seemingly stuck with no idea how to progress, there's a good chance this little key was the culprit!

Despite keeping most of the original dungeon's layout intact, the remake has made things considerably easier by removing this easily missed Small Key altogether. This means players no longer have to spend ages retracing their steps and wondering whether they've somehow managed to softlock their game.

Of course, the Water Temple is still a memorable dungeon, and I'm certainly not complaining about a more streamlined experience. But I do find it funny that an entire generation of players had to suffer through those confusing corridors just so newcomers could have a slightly more pleasant time! You're welcome, younger Zelda fans. We fought in the trenches so you wouldn't have to.

#4277. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4274. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

#4273. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

#4272. Xbox Will Make You Watch Three Minutes of Ads for Just 30 Minutes of Gaming

Microsoft has found another way to make money from Xbox, and this time, you'll be paying with your time rather than your wallet. The company has detailed its ad-supported cloud gaming service, which offers 30 minutes of gameplay in exchange for watching three minutes of commercials.

The service is being marketed to advertisers as Xbox Video for Brands. For gamers, it's an alternative to the subscription-based Xbox Cloud Gaming service, allowing eligible users to stream games without an active Game Pass subscription.

A rising number of players are citing prohibitive monthly costs as their reason for canceling gaming subscriptions.

Free access to cloud gaming certainly sounds appealing, but half an hour isn't much time, especially when you have to sit through three minutes of ads before you can even start playing.

In a November 12 announcement, Microsoft confirmed that its ad-supported cloud gaming service will feature a three-minute pre-roll advertising block before each 30-minute gaming session.

These advertisements will be full-screen and non-skippable, although they won't interrupt active gameplay. Instead, they'll appear before the session begins, during the cloud-loading process.

Microsoft describes this as an opportunity for advertisers to reach gamers just as they're preparing to play. The company believes that this makes Xbox an attractive advertising platform, since the audience is already engaged and ready to start gaming.

But from a gamer's perspective, three minutes of advertisements for just half an hour of gameplay doesn't sound particularly generous. The ads won't interrupt your gameplay, but the 30-minute session limit certainly will.

Consider how much time you might spend doing something relatively mundane in an RPG or an open-world game, whether that's exploring a new area, completing a quest, or simply getting sidetracked. You could easily spend most of your allotted time without making much progress.

The ads won't interrupt your gameplay, but the 30-minute session limit certainly will.

To be clear, Microsoft isn't adding commercial breaks to games you've already purchased. The advertisements are limited to this optional cloud gaming tier, and they'll play before you start gaming rather than interrupting an ongoing session.

The announcement also leaves some details unclear, including whether every region and session will have precisely the same advertising requirements.

What's rather disappointing about the newly announced arrangement is that Microsoft's earlier ad-supported cloud gaming tests were considerably more generous.

When the company began testing the service with Xbox Insiders in July, users could access one-hour gaming sessions after watching advertisements. Earlier reporting indicated that these introductory ads lasted approximately two minutes. That's twice the gameplay time, with fewer advertisements to sit through.

The new arrangement looks considerably less appealing by comparison, although free access still has its uses. If you occasionally want to try a game without committing to a Game Pass subscription, even 30 minutes might be enough. For anything more substantial, however, the time limit could become frustrating rather quickly.

There's also the question of what happens when those 30 minutes run out. Can you immediately start another session after watching more ads, or will you have to wait in another queue? And how smoothly will the service handle resuming a game after the previous session expires?

Microsoft hasn't explained these details in its latest announcement, so we'll have to see how the system works in practice.

The introduction of advertisements is part of a much larger restructuring of Xbox Cloud Gaming. As DualShockers previously reported, Microsoft has also introduced pay-as-you-go cloud gaming packages, allowing you to purchase streaming time without subscribing to Game Pass.

The introductory prices include $3.99 for 10 hours, $7.99 for 25 hours, and $11.99 for 50 hours of gameplay. These packages offer ad-free streaming, and the purchased hours remain available until they're used.

Meanwhile, Game Pass subscriptions now have monthly cloud gaming allowances, with Ultimate receiving 15 hours, Premium receiving 10 hours, and Essential receiving five hours. If you exhaust your included hours, you can purchase additional time or use the ad-supported service where available.

Microsoft has justified these changes by pointing to the growing costs of cloud gaming as more people use the service. Streaming certainly has its advantages, particularly if you don't own a powerful gaming PC or a modern console. And with the next Xbox reportedly carrying an eye-watering price tag, being able to play without buying new hardware might sound even more appealing.

But Microsoft's approach to the service is changing. Instead of simply treating cloud gaming as another benefit of the Xbox ecosystem, the company is increasingly dividing it into subscriptions, purchased hours, and advertising-supported sessions.

And while the latter doesn't cost anything, you're still paying with your time. Watching a few advertisements to try a game might be reasonable enough, but sitting through three minutes of commercials every time you want another half hour of gameplay sounds considerably less appealing.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has hinted that Xbox Game Pass prices could go down in the future, though this could be part of a shift to digital ownership.

#4271. It's Official, Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Has Sold Over 5 Million Copies In 4 Days

Nintendo has announced that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has sold a total of 5.2 million units in just four days.

This number includes 810,000 copies sold in Japan alone, and makes Ocarina of Time the fastest-selling Nintendo-published Switch 2 game since the console's launch. For added context, the N64 original sold an overall total of 7.6 million units, according to Video Game Sales wiki.

This also makes it the second highest-selling Switch 2 game, with initial sales putting it above Donkey Kong Bananza's lifetime sales at 5.05 million (as of 30th September 2026). The best-selling Switch 2 game remains Mario Kart World at 16.48 million.

It's not clear what the digital/physical split is at the time of writing, though we should have a slightly better picture of this once Famitsu releases the Japanese boxed charts later this week.

Nintendo Co., Ltd. (HQ: Kyoto, Minami-ku, Japan; President and Representative Director: Shuntaro Furukawa, “Nintendo” hereafter) announced that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 sold over 5.2 million units worldwide (including 810,000 units sold in Japan) in the first four days following its launch on November 5, 2026.

This is the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2, released worldwide on November 5, is a full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, originally released for Nintendo 64 in 1998. Link travels between two time periods, as Young Link and Adult Link, making use of different abilities and items available in each period to progress through his adventure. Developed for Nintendo Switch 2, the game features reimagined visuals and enhanced playability, while preserving the experience of the original game.

The game also supports ZELDA NOTES, a service available within the Nintendo Switch App for compatible smart devices. By using ZELDA NOTES, players can access a variety of features that support gameplay.

In the UK, it was confirmed that Ocarina of Time was the second biggest physical launch in series history, coming in just behind Tears of the Kingdom. It stormed to the top of the charts to become the biggest physical video game launch of 2026 (so far – hi, GTA).

As for our review, we awarded Ocarina of Time a 9/10, stating it to be "the best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time":

"Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a stellar reimagining of the original, one that completely revamps the experience with stunning visuals, modernised gameplay, and vastly improved audio. Despite some minor blemishes, this is comfortably the most visually stunning work Nintendo has ever put out, and it’s unquestionably the best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time."

@larryisaman I couldn’t agree more. This has genuinely baffled me. The original was super easy combat wise, and I mean super easy. You know what both the original and the remake have in common, though? Both have moments where it just feels epic when fighting - the boss music and some of the boss battles are just so thrilling. OOT has never been challenging and so many are lamenting the loss of challenge that was never there… I’m baffled. Also, the remake adds some phases and also increases the health of a lot of the enemies. I agree with you and I am so confused at this “lack of challenge in fights” narrative.

Someone else said so why have fights at all? The reason is that it’s a game about a young man who fights to save the world from evil… but this isn’t a fighting game, and the fighting is far from the main objective or theme of the game. Ocarina is a package and it is a beautifully made one at that.

It's easily Nintendo's best remake yet. Predicting a 10+ million seller throughout the Switch 2's life.

May Nintendo understand that there was nothing wrong with the classic design philosophy. Love the open air games, but entries of this scope are also fine enough.

Comments about the game being easier in the remake should also factor in the impact from the improved controls. It's like Metroid Prime remaster had easier sections thanks to the improved aiming.

An amazing achievement! Although we need to give some credit to the success of BOTW / TOTK getting Zelda out there and into the hands of the broader audience first.

Now that job is done, we have the reigniting of classical elements for those that never experienced the original formula, alongside the smarter play of showing the newest audience (and indeed the younger staff that developed the remake) what made Zelda so beloved in the first place.

@Yoshi3 I still genuinely don’t think this is the way to go, otherwise the series will stagnate and die. There are better Zelda clones out there and Nintendo can’t survive on its nostalgia alone.

What we need is for elements of both older and newer gameplay mechanics to evolve the franchise. This idea was somewhat close in concept with Echoes of Wisdom.

Nintendo have already said they aren’t abandoning the open air exploration element in future games, so it’s just going to be really important that they find a way to bring back in some of the more classic elements (Dungeons, specific items to unlock that manage progression, and turn down the survival element a tad) to marriage a really good mix and innovate.

TOTK was getting there in terms of it’s Dungeons and Temples, but they still weren’t on the same level of intricate design as past games. I don’t know the answer to this however, so hopefully Nintendo will find a solution with whatever comes next.

@ABmajora yeah, Zelda fights have generally focused on puzzle solving rather than reaction timing.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Avengers: Endgame Encore is set to hit Disney Plus on November 13, and you'll be able to rewatch those wild post-credits scenes as many times you want.

The film was re-released in September in honor of the film's seven-year anniversary, but also to get Marvel fans hyped for Avengers: Doomsday. The Encore version of the film is more or less the same except for four bonus scenes added to the end credits. The scenes in question are: Loki goes back to the past to visit Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter; Doctor Doom has captured Hulk after the events of Spider-Man: Brand New Day; an incursion is coming to destroy the Fox X-Men universe; and Tony Stark appears to be making a Doctor Doom Mask (which is terribly confusing and also lends credence to the rumor that Downey isn't actually playing Doom after all).

These scenes are meant to bridge the gap between Endgame and Doomsday, and will therefore not appear in the latter. We can also assume that that absolutely wild surprise post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest will also not be in Doomsday, and is another 'gap-bridging' moment.

You can also check out the Avengers: Endgame Encore landing page on Disney Plus should you feel like refreshing the page until the movie finally drops.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in the UK December 16 and in the US on December 18. For more, check out our guides to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#4268. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

We’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.
